trial_name.text: RLY5016-301 (two-part, single-blind Phase 3; Part A treatment phase and Part B randomized withdrawal phase each serving as one of two pivotal studies)

citations.quote: Study RLY5016-301 was a two-part, single-blind, Phase 3 study of Veltassa in 243 subjects with hyperkalemia and CKD. Each part of Study RLY5016-301 (Part A and Part B) serves as one of the two pivotal studies for marketing approval evaluation.

design.text: Two-part, single-blind study conducted under Special Protocol Assessment: Part A was a single-arm, two dose-level, 4-week open-label treatment phase; Part B was a randomized, placebo-controlled, 8-week assessment of withdrawal of Veltassa in Part A responders with baseline potassium >=5.5 mEq/L.

citations.quote: Study RLY5016-301 was a two-part, single-blind, phase 3 study evaluating the efficacy and safety of patiromer for the treatment of hyperkalemia. The study was conducted under Special Protocol Assessment.

Part A of the study was a single arm with two dose level, 4-week treatment phase study to assess if Veltassa achieved a clinically meaningful reduction in serum potassium levels in subjects with hyperkalemia.

Part B was a randomized, placebo-controlled, 8-week assessment of the withdrawal of RLY5016. Subjects with a baseline serum potassium \ge 5.5 mEq/L (central laboratory) at the beginning of Part A were entered into Part B of the study if they had responded to the 4 weeks of treatment with RLY5016 during Part A

population.text: Subjects with hyperkalemia and chronic kidney disease (CKD); 243 subjects enrolled at 71 sites in 10 countries.

citations.quote: Study RLY5016-301 was a two-part, single-blind, Phase 3 study of Veltassa in 243 subjects with hyperkalemia and CKD.
Two hundred forty-three (243) subjects were enrolled in 71 sites in 10 countries including Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Georgia, Hungary, Italy, Serbia, Slovenia, Ukraine, and United States.

endpoint.text: Part A primary endpoint: change in serum potassium (central laboratory) from Part A baseline to Part A Week 4. Part B primary endpoint: change from Part B baseline serum potassium during the randomized withdrawal phase.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint for Part A was the change in serum potassium (central laboratory) from Part A baseline to the Part A Week 4 visit.
The primary efficacy endpoint for Part B was the change from Part B baseline (central laboratory) serum potassium to serum potassium (central laboratory) at either:

result.text: Part A: overall mean change in serum potassium from baseline to Week 4 was -1.01 mEq/L (95% CI -1.07, -0.95; p<0.001 vs zero). Part B: estimated median change was +0.72 mEq/L on placebo vs 0.00 mEq/L on Veltassa; difference 0.72 mEq/L (95% CI 0.46, 0.99; p<0.001).

citations.quote: The primary efficacy analysis in Part A of Study RLY5016-301 gave an overall mean change in serum potassium from Part A Baseline to Week 4 of -1.01 (with se of 0.031) mEq/L [95% CI: (-1.07, -0.95)], that gave p < 0.001 in the comparison to zero.

The estimated median changes from Part B baseline in serum potassium in the placebo and the Veltassa group were increases of 0.72 and 0 mEq/L, respectively. The estimated difference in median change from Part B baseline (placebo minus Veltassa) was 0.72 mEq/L with 95% CI (0.46, 0.99); with p<0.001 for between-group difference in mean ranks of change.

indication.text: Veltassa is indicated for the treatment of hyperkalemia; it should not be used as an emergency treatment for life-threatening hyperkalemia because of its delayed onset of action.

citations.quote: Veltassa is indicated for the treatment of hyperkalemia.
Limitation of Use: Veltassa should not be used as an emergency treatment for life-threatening hyperkalemia because of its delayed onset of action [see *Pharmacodynamics (12.2)*].

target_moa.text: Veltassa (patiromer) is a non-absorbed cation-exchange polymer with a calcium-sorbitol counterion; it binds potassium in the lumen of the colon (exchanging calcium for potassium), increasing fecal potassium excretion and thereby lowering serum potassium.

citations.quote: Veltassa is a non-absorbed, cation exchange polymer that contains a calcium-sorbitol counterion.
Patiromer is a cation-exchange polymer1 that binds potassium in the lumen of the colon, thereby increasing fecal potassium excretion and lowering serum potassium levels.
Calcium ions are exchanged with potassium ions.

modality.text: Small molecule / non-absorbed polymer (cation-exchange polymer; not systemically absorbed)

citations.quote: The active ingredient is patiromer sorbitex calcium which consists of the active moiety, patiromer, a non-absorbed potassium-binding polymer, and a calcium-sorbitol counterion.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2%) were constipation (7.2%), hypomagnesemia (5.3%), diarrhea (4.8%), nausea (2.3%), abdominal discomfort (2.0%) and flatulence (2.0%) in patients treated with Veltassa (N=666). Hypomagnesemia was reported in 5.3% of patients.

detail.text: WARNING: BINDING TO OTHER ORAL MEDICATIONS — Veltassa binds to many orally administered medications, which could decrease their absorption and reduce effectiveness; administer other oral medications at least 6 hours before or 6 hours after Veltassa.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: BINDING TO OTHER ORAL MEDICATIONS

Veltassa binds to many orally administered medications, which could decrease their absorption and reduce their effectiveness. Administer other oral medications at least 6 hours before or 6 hours after Veltassa. Choose Veltassa or the other oral medication if adequate dosing separation is not possible [see *Dosage and Administration (2.1), Warnings and Precautions (5.1) and Drug Interactions (7)*].

summary.text: Veltassa received a standard (full) approval via NDA 205739 submitted October 21, 2014 with a PDUFA goal date of October 21, 2015; efficacy was based on a single two-part Phase 3 trial (RLY5016-301) conducted under Special Protocol Assessment, with Part A and the Part B randomized withdrawal phase each serving as a pivotal study. The application was not referred to an advisory committee, and deferred pediatric studies were required under PREA.
